title: Units and Measurement: Chapter Introduction
subject: Physics
objective: A number alone means nothing: every measurement is a number and a unit. The chapter builds the SI system, significant figures and dimensions, the base of all physics.

fill.q: Every measurement is written as a number and a ____.
The SI base unit of mass is the ____.
The SI base unit of electric current is the ____.
Checking a formula by comparing the dimensions of its two sides uses the principle of ____ of dimensions.

tf.q: The newton is an SI base unit.
tf.explain: It is a derived unit: 1 N = 1 kg m s⁻².

tf.q: The kelvin is the SI base unit of temperature.
tf.explain: It is one of the 7 base units.

tf.q: A dimensionally correct formula is always physically correct.
tf.explain: Dimensions cannot check pure-number constants such as ½.

tf.q: The Mars Climate Orbiter was lost because of a unit mix-up.
tf.explain: Thrust data in pound-force seconds was read as newton-seconds.

ar.a: v = u + at² is dimensionally wrong.
ar.r: The term at² has dimensions [L], not [LT⁻¹].
ar.explain: R is exactly why the two sides disagree.

ar.a: The newton is a derived unit.
ar.r: Every SI unit other than the 7 base units is built from the base units.

mcq.q: Which is NOT an SI base unit?
mcq.explain: The newton is derived from kg, m and s.

mcq.q: The SI base unit of luminous intensity is the:
mcq.explain: Candela is one of the 7 base units.

mcq.q: The number of significant figures in 0.0250 is:
mcq.explain: Leading zeros do not count; the final zero after the decimal point does: 2, 5, 0.

mcq.q: The Mars Climate Orbiter mix-up was between:
mcq.explain: One team used pound-force, the other expected newton.

num.q: Write 1 newton in SI base units and give its dimensions.

num.answer: Every term is [L], so the formula is dimensionally correct.

num.q: 1 pound-force = 4.45 N. Convert a thrust of 10 pound-force to newton.

short.q: Why is a number alone not a measurement?
short.solution: A number says how many, the unit says of what. 5 m, 5 s and 5 kg are completely different quantities; without the unit the number has no meaning, as the Mars Climate Orbiter loss showed.

short.q: What does the number of significant figures in a reading tell us?
short.solution: It shows how precise and reliable the reading is: 2.54 cm (3 significant figures) is more precise than 2.5 cm (2 significant figures).

match.explain: These are 5 of the 7 SI base units; the other 2 are kelvin (temperature) and mole (amount of substance).
